submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path (retraction lane, extending sweep coverage per handoff 2026-08-08b §3.3)
rationale:
The review-queue sweep drains parked work items by re-running the check that filed them. claims_unverified was not covered and nothing else closed it: on live clients_db, SELECT status, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='claims_unverified' AND status IN ('complete','verified') returned zero rows, no row of the type carried a deploy_result payload, and the producer sets HandlerAgent to "" by design, so there was no dispatch path, no handler and no revalidator. 23 items across 7 sites sat at needs_human_review permanently, by construction.

This change registers a revalidator for the type. It extracts the emit-side scan into a shared ScanDeployedClaims so the revalidator re-runs the identical predicate rather than a second copy of it, and has that scan report how much it examined so that 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'. Two gates stand between a clean re-scan and a closed item: the page's copy must have changed since the finding was filed, and every text the finding cited must have gone from the slot it was cited from. Both must pass. Everything that cannot answer returns 'unknown', which is non-terminal and leaves the item where a human can still see it.

STATUS OF EACH EDIT, because this plan describes code that mostly already exists. Shipped and running, verified at HEAD: edit 1 (check_unverified_claims.go:356 ScanDeployedClaims, :306 LoadEvidenceBase, :239 ClaimsPageScan), edit 2 (revalidate_unverified_claims.go:93, :240), edit 3 (revalidate_review_queue_action.go:229), edit 5 (revalidate_review_queue_test.go:189), edit 7's NewestComponentUpdate (check_unverified_claims.go:260), edit 8's CreatedAt (revalidate_review_queue_action.go:141). Edit 4's tests ship alongside them. Committed but NOT yet rolled: edit 6's claim-granular gate (revalidate_unverified_claims.go:302) and edit 7's ExaminedTextBySlot (check_unverified_claims.go:283) at 58bede8d5, and edit 8's loader contract (revalidate_review_queue_action.go:167) at ea18664f3. Review follows the change here rather than preceding it, because HEAD is shared on this tree and any session's build ships any committed work, so no thread can hold code back. That is the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 section 2, and it is now readable in the corpus this council uses: SELECT count(*) FROM doc_notes WHERE body ILIKE '%ordering exemption%' returns 5 rows carrying the phrase 'CONDITION (1) OF THE ORDERING EXEMPTION IS RETIRED' verbatim. It had zero rows until 2026-08-12; a previous round cited the ruling with no way for a reviewer to check it, and that was a fair objection.

NOT VERIFIABLE FROM A REVIEWER'S TOOLING, marked rather than asserted. The deploy statements above rest on a probe of the running binary (kubectl exec ... grep -ac on /proc/1/exe, with the exit code captured) and on git ancestry. The single-producer claim rests on a code_symbols query. Neither the pod nor code_symbols is in a reviewer's schema. These are this submitter's measurements, given with the exact commands so they can be re-run by someone who has that access; a seat should treat them as unverified rather than as established fact.

One correction carried forward, because it changed the argument. Round 1 claimed two converging producers and invoked the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 section 1 as authority for shipping without an RFC. There is one producer, so that ruling never applied. check_unverified_claims_stats.go registers no check, has no init() and emits no WorkItemSpec; its scanStoredStatClaims is called only from inside ScanDeployedClaims. The change is simpler than round 1 described and no longer leans on a ruling that did not cover it.

plan.summary: Register a claims_unverified revalidator in the review-queue sweep. Extract the emit-side claims scan into a shared ScanDeployedClaims so the revalidator re-runs the identical predicate instead of a second copy, and have that scan report how much it examined so 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'. Move the locked-component skip out of SQL into Go so pinned components are counted rather than silently dropped. Two gates guard closure: the page's copy must have changed since the finding was filed, and every text the finding cited must have gone from the slot it was cited from. The verdict ladder is a pure function with every arm unit-tested.

edits.rationale: Extract the page/site query and the claim scans out of UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run into an exported ScanDeployedClaims used by both ends, and export the evidence-base loader. ClaimsPageScan carries ComponentsExamined and ComponentsSkippedLocked because len(Findings)==0 otherwise collapses three states into one: the copy was fixed, nothing was read, and only locked components were read. Only the first may close an item. The locked-component skip moves from SQL to Go: the page query carried AND pc.locked_at IS NULL, which dropped pinned rows before anything could count them, so a page whose only claims sat in a locked component was indistinguishable from one that had been cleaned up. Emitted output is unchanged, because Run filters to pages that carry findings, so the work items this check files are byte-identical. ClaimFinding is a type alias for the unexported unverifiedClaimFinding: the revalidator must name the type it iterates, and the unexported spelling has about 20 use sites including this package's tests, so aliasing avoids churn that buys nothing. The emit side is rewired in this same edit rather than a separate one because the plan is capped at 8 edits and these are one refactor of one file.

The drain itself. Database glue is split from a pure verdict ladder so every arm is testable without a database. Ladder order is load-bearing: 'still carries claims' is answered before 'some components were locked', or a page that still asserts a banned claim would be reported as unreadable rather than as still holding. Safe direction throughout: a wrong still_holds costs a human glance, a wrong resolved closes a live finding about an unsupported factual claim, so every arm that cannot answer returns unknown, which is non-terminal. The missing-page_id arm is where the grouped site-chrome item lands: its item_key is the literal claims:site_components and its spec carries surface, not page_id. The item_key prefix is never parsed for a page id.
One map entry is the whole wiring. coveredItemTypes() is derived from reviewRevalidators, so registering the revalidator widens what the sweep selects in the same edit, with no second list to drift.

Every ladder arm exercised without a database, plus both gates' own tests. Two assertions are properties rather than cases: nothing reaches resolved without having examined a component, and a fully-read clean page whose copy moved must resolve, because a revalidator that can only say still_holds is the armed-but-inert shape this lane keeps finding elsewhere. The claim-granular tests pass changedAfter deliberately, so the timestamp gate is satisfied and only the new gate can refuse; a test that passed because the timestamp refused would assert nothing. Two behaviours that were previously assumed are now pinned, because both fail in the unsafe direction: ExtractAssertionText does see plain text and content_data JSON (a claim it could not see would read as removed, which closes the item), and a token appearing only in a class name or data attribute no longer holds an item open. TestParkedReviewItemSelectAndScanAgree holds the shared loader's contract. Every guard here has been mutation-tested: disabling each refusal arm, dropping created_at from the SELECT, adding a column without a destination, making the match case-sensitive, and reverting to a raw-markup search each fail exactly the test written to catch them, and the restored code is green.
This test pins the covered set and fails on any change, telling the author to update it and say why. It fired, as designed. The want list gains claims_unverified.

edits.symbol: unverifiedClaimsVerdict (copy-changed and claim-granular gates), flaggedClaim, flaggedClaimsFromSpec, claimStillOnPage
edits.rationale:
Two gates, both required. The copy-changed gate is the owner's ruling of 2026-08-09, answering the compliance seat across two rounds: resolved requires positive evidence that the page moved, an examined component whose page_components.updated_at is later than the item's created_at, so a register edit alone cannot retract a finding. The zero-filedAt case is a separate arm because x.After(time.Time{}) is true for any real timestamp; folding it into the comparison would make an item with no known filing date close on any component edit however old, the exact inverse of the gate. That defect was briefly real, with the header comment claiming the correct behaviour while the code did not, and the property test caught the difference.

The claim-granular gate narrows it further, answering the same seat's remaining objection. The copy-changed gate proves the page moved, not that the flagged claim was addressed: a typo fix or an edit to an adjacent field satisfies it. So resolved now also requires every text the finding cited to be absent from the slot it was cited from, read from the item's own spec.findings[].matched. Three refusal arms, all non-terminal: the text is still present, the cited slot was not among the components examined, or the item records no usable finding text.

The comparison uses the matched token rather than the cited snippet, and that choice was measured. Against the population where the answer is known, items still holding where the claim is by definition on the page, a slot-scoped snippet comparison found the claim in 18 of 41 cases and the token in 40 of 41. A snippet breaks on any whitespace or markup change, and in this gate a broken match reads as 'the copy changed', which grants closure, so the snippet version would have failed open on about half of all claims.

The search runs over datahelpers.ExtractAssertionText, the same extraction the emit side scans, so both ends of an item's life judge the same text. On the live population that changes nothing measurable: 2 false refusals either way, 40 of 41 sensitivity either way. It is made for parity and reuse, not because it moved a number.

Both gates are ANDed; risks item 3 puts the open question of whether the claim check should replace the timestamp to the owner rather than deciding it here.

Supplies both gates' evidence from the scan that is already reading these rows, so there is no second query and no second predicate. NewestComponentUpdate and ExaminedTextBySlot are tracked for examined components only: a locked component's content was not read, so nothing may be concluded from its presence or absence. ExaminedTextBySlot is keyed by slot rather than concatenated page-wide, and that is measured rather than assumed. Page-wide, a bare unregistered_number token such as '5' or '26' matches somewhere in almost any page's markup: across the 8 closed items a page-wide search reported 7 of 18 cited texts still present, every one of them 1 to 4 characters long, while scoped to the slot the count is 2. A page-wide gate would refuse nearly everything while appearing rigorous. Components sharing a slot name are concatenated, so a finding is judged against everything read under its own slot.

parkedReviewItem gains CreatedAt, which is what the copy-changed gate compares against. Without it filedAt arrives as the zero value and the gate can never reach resolved. It is one more column from a row loadParkedReviewItems already reads.

The SELECT and the Scan are one contract, and this edit makes that mechanical rather than advisory. loadParkedReviewItems serves all six covered item types, so a column added to one half and not the other is a runtime scan error rather than a compile error, and it fails every revalidator in the sweep at once, not only this one. parkedReviewItemColumns is the SELECT list and parkedReviewItemScanDests returns one destination per entry; TestParkedReviewItemSelectAndScanAgree fails when they diverge, and it names created_at explicitly so dropping that column fails a test instead of silently sending every item to the unknown arm for ever. The query text is unchanged. This replaces a warning comment, after two seats pointed out that an earlier version of this submission argued a comment is not a control on a shared tree and then offered one as the mitigation.
edits.sketch:
type parkedReviewItem struct {
	...
	CreatedAt time.Time  // for the claims_unverified copy-changed gate
}

// ⚠ THIS SELECT AND THE rows.Scan BELOW ARE ONE CONTRACT
query := fmt.Sprintf(`
	SELECT id::text, site_id, item_type, COALESCE(item_key, ''), COALESCE(spec, '{}'::jsonb),
	       created_at
	FROM site_work_items
	WHERE status IN (%s) AND item_type IN (%s)`, ...)
...
rows.Scan(&it.ID, &it.SiteID, &it.ItemType, &it.ItemKey, &specJSON, &it.CreatedAt)

plan.risks:
1) Behaviour change, stated plainly: claims_unverified items can now be closed without a human. The type was designed HITL-terminal and two open bug files (033, 083) tabulate it as parked work, so their counts move; both owners have been told rather than merely measured. Retraction never edits copy and never dispatches a rewrite, but it is still a machine closing a human-review row about a factual claim.

2) The evidence_base register is data, so a finding can stop tripping the check because the standard moved rather than the copy. Both gates exist for this. The copy-changed gate (owner ruling 2026-08-09) requires an examined component edited after filing. The claim-granular gate requires the cited text to have gone from its own slot. A register edit alone closes nothing.

3) OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER, deliberately not decided here. The two gates are ANDed. The claim check is the stronger evidence of the two: a token that has left its slot proves the copy moved, where a timestamp only asserts it. So it could stand in for the timestamp rather than be added to it. Requiring both can refuse a genuinely fixed page whose updated_at was never bumped. It is left ANDed because adding a condition in front of an owner-mandated control needs no new ruling, whereas removing his comparison would.

4) The gate cannot detect a claim that was rephrased rather than removed. New wording asserting the same unsupported thing passes the token check and is caught only if the re-scan itself flags it. The re-scan is the backstop, which is why the revalidator re-runs the emit side's own predicate instead of a second copy.

5) Residual false refusals, measured rather than estimated: on the 8 items closed to date, 2 of 18 cited texts still match inside their own slot, both of them 1-2 character numbers. Those items would now refuse instead of closing. That is the safe direction (a wrong 'unknown' costs a human glance; a wrong 'resolved' closes a live factual-claim finding) but it is a real cost, and the type will drain more slowly than the population suggests.

6) loadParkedReviewItems is the shared loader for all six covered item types. Edit 8 adds a column to its SELECT and a destination to its rows.Scan; a mismatch is a runtime scan error, not a compile error, and it fails every revalidator in the sweep at once rather than only this one. This is the widest blast radius in the change. It is now held by a test (TestParkedReviewItemSelectAndScanAgree) rather than by a comment, after two seats pointed out that an earlier version of this submission argued 'a comment is not a control' and then offered one.

7) voice_tells has the identical moving-standard hole and gets neither gate. That is deliberate: it is live and council-approved and its surface is style rather than truth, which is the distinction the seats themselves drew. It is now tracked at features_open/032_FEATURE_voice_tells_needs_the_claim_granular_gate_too.md, with the shared-helper approach and the instruction to measure before building, rather than left as an accepted risk with no artefact.

8) The locked-component skip moved from SQL to Go, so rows the query previously discarded now reach the scan loop and are skipped there. Emitted output is unchanged by construction (a locked row continues before any scan runs), but this is the class of change where widening what reaches a function breaks it unedited, so the skip must stay ahead of the scans in any future edit to that loop.

9) The scan has no page-status filter and this change does not add one, preserving the emit side's predicate exactly. Measured: page status across the population is active 19, archived 2, deleted 2, so an item can resolve on a page nobody serves. The 2 deleted pages refuse via the nil-scan arm.

10) The locked-component arms are unexercised on live data (has_locked_components is 0), so they are reasoned and unit-tested rather than observed. They exist because the population will change and because a scan that examined nothing returns the same empty findings list as a page that was genuinely cleaned up.
